items.title: Boris Cherny: We Cut 80% of Claude Code’s Prompt
items.title_he: Boris Cherny: מחקנו 80% מה-prompt של Claude Code
items.description:
Fresh off the launch of Opus 5, Claude Code creator Boris Cherny joins Diana Hu at Startup School 2026 to talk about what the newest models can do, how Claude Code came to be, and what it means to build products when the underlying capabilities keep accelerating.

Transcript: https://www.ycrootaccess.com/p/boris-cherny-building-claude-code

Apply to Y Combinator: https://www.ycombinator.com/apply
Work at a startup: https://www.ycombinator.com/jobs

Chapters:
00:00 — Intro
00:07 — What Makes Opus 5 Different
02:06 — Solving Prompt Injection
03:21 — Why Claude Code Deleted 80% of Its System Prompt
06:37 — Press Delete on Your AI Product
07:20 — How to Rebuild Your System Prompt
10:30 — Product Overhang and “Unhobbling” AI
14:26 — Give Claude Harder Problems
19:32 — Prompt Engineering Is Changing
21:57 — The Two-Week Claude Code Prompt
24:42 — Running Thousands of AI Agents
30:15 — Coding Is (Almost) Solved
32:20 — What Every CS Student Should Still Learn
items.blurb_he: זו שיחה על הבמה ב-Startup School 2026 של Y Combinator. Boris Cherny, היוצר של Claude Code ב-Anthropic, משוחח עם Diana Hu מ-YC. השיחה הוקלטה יום אחרי השקת Opus 5. אין בה שקפים, רק שאלות ותשובות. השיחה עוברת על היכולות החדשות של המודל, על ההחלטה למחוק יותר מ-80% מה-system prompt של Claude Code, על הרעיון של product overhang, ועל הדרך שבה הצוות מריץ היום אלפי agents בבת אחת.
items.speakers: Boris Cherny, Diana Hu

items.description:
From the rapid rise of Claude Code to a future where agents can rewrite their own harnesses, collaborate across teams, and operate across cloud and local environments, the way we build software is changing extraordinarily fast. In this episode, Anthropic’s Thariq Shihipar joins swyx and Vibhu to unpack how power users are actually working with Claude Code today, why prompting remains a high-skill discipline, and where Anthropic thinks the agent harness is headed next.

We go deep on Claude Code’s evolving interface: Ask User Question and elicitation, artifacts as persistent generative interfaces, Claude Tag for multiplayer agent workflows, Projects, model effort, implementation notes, and the new Claude Mods system for customizing the harness itself. Thariq explains why Claude.md may eventually disappear, why the smartest model could also become the cheapest model for many tasks, and why mutable software could become a new paradigm for how applications are built and customized.

The conversation then turns to agent security and Anthropic’s “Pacing the Frontier” argument. Thariq walks through recent incidents where agents discovered unexpected ways to communicate, exploit infrastructure, reverse-engineer benchmark scorers, and chain vulnerabilities together. We discuss sandboxing, prompt injection, autonomous agents, interpretability, constitutional classifiers, probes, fallbacks, Auto Mode, and why securing increasingly capable agents may become one of the defining engineerin

items.title: What It Actually Takes to Build a Software Factory — Tereza Tížková, Factory
items.title_he: מה באמת נדרש כדי לבנות Software Factory
items.description:
Everyone is talking about software factories, but few people are building one. Tereza Tížková of Factory, which runs software factories for enterprises like EY and Adobe, defines one as the whole software lifecycle run autonomously: collecting signals, prioritizing, building, validating and improving. It's not just a swarm of coding agents, because writing code is the easy part.

She lays out three principles. Stay agnostic: fit how your team already works, and route between models automatically (Factory's conservative benchmark shows about 25% savings). Stay autonomous: Factory's Missions run for hours or even weeks, with a real customer example running 16. Worker agents run in sequence instead of a swarm, so each starts with fresh context, and validators check code they didn't write. One of those validators actually clicks through the app. Keep improving: a deferred context engine cuts token use by 50% or more, and an agent-readiness check keeps AI from making a messy codebase worse. She closes on what's left for humans: deciding what to build, not how.

items.description:
Modern AI systems are evolving from single prompts into networks of collaborating agents that plan, delegate tasks, invoke tools, and coordinate actions across distributed systems. But orchestrating multiple agents introduces the same architectural challenges you've faced with microservices: shared state, retries, partial failures, consistency, and long-running workflows.
In this session, we explore patterns for building durable multi-agent systems. We'll examine orchestration vs. choreography, agent coordination models, workflow durability, and failure handling, and show how Lambda Durable Functions implement them. You'll leave with practical frameworks for designing reliable, observable multi-agent architectures on AWS.

items.title_he: ECS בלי לנהל שרתים: Managed Instances ו-Express Mode
items.description:
"Amazon ECS offers multiple compute options that enable architects to optimize for performance, cost, and operational requirements. This session provides a comprehensive guide to using AWS Fargate, Amazon ECS Managed Instances, and self-managed EC2 with Amazon ECS. We will dive into the technical architecture, operational models, and cost implications of each compute type through real world scenarios.

Amazon ECS Express Mode simplifies container deployment by turning hours of configuration into seconds of execution. We will explore how it enables to deploy a production-ready containerized application with just one command."

items.title: vLLM on AWS: testing to production and everything in between
items.title_he: vLLM על AWS: מבדיקה ועד פרודקשן
items.description: This session explores practical architectural patterns for deploying and scaling large language models (LLMs) in production environments. We'll walk through a comprehensive journey from initial testing to production deployment, covering essential steps including model evaluation with vLLM, performance benchmarking, and optimization techniques. Attendees will learn how to implement efficient autoscaling solutions using Ray and vLLM, compare different inference servers like Triton and vLLM, and understand their trade-offs. The session concludes with a deep dive into productionalization using AIBrix, providing attendees with actionable insights for building robust, scalable LLM infrastructures. Suitable for ML engineers and architects working on LLM deployments.

items.title: Simplify your Kubernetes journey with Amazon EKS Capabilities
items.title_he: לפשט את מסע ה-Kubernetes עם EKS Capabilities
items.description: Amazon EKS has launched new managed Kubernetes capabilities for workload orchestration and resource management, to help you build and scale with Kubernetes on AWS. Kubernetes is a powerful standard for scheduling workloads, but supporting multiple environments, managing fleets of clusters, and maintaining configuration at scale all present challenges and friction. This typically results in installing and managing open source components yourself. In this session, learn how you can leverage Amazon EKS to more easily meet these foundational needs, with AWS doing the heavy lifting so that you can focus on building and shipping software, rather than managing and scaling platforms.

items.title: Resilience at Scale on Amazon EKS: Networking, Security, and Compute
items.title_he: רזיליינס בסקייל על Amazon EKS
items.description: How do you architect Amazon EKS to meet your SLA requirements while optimizing for resilience and efficiency? This session discusses architectural best practices across key pillars: resilience, networking, security, and compute optimization. Explore approaches for traffic routing, network segmentation, and tenant isolation. Learn patterns for achieving high availability from single-region to global scale. Discover techniques for optimizing compute resources and workload placement. Walk away with an understanding based on AWS EKS Best Practices and actionable patterns you can implement immediately.
